content.prompt:
Show that triangle $ABC$ is isosceles. 
Give full reasoning for each stage of your working.

answer.short: $\angle CAB=\angle ACB=52^{\circ}$, so $BC=AB$ and $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=180^{\circ}-104^{\circ}\\\angle ABC&=76^{\circ}\end{aligned}$$Angles on a straight line sum to 180°.

$$\begin{aligned}\angle CAB&=\angle FCA\\\angle CAB&=52^{\circ}\end{aligned}$$Alternate angles on parallel lines are equal.

$$\begin{aligned}\angle ACB&=180^{\circ}-76^{\circ}-52^{\circ}\\\angle ACB&=52^{\circ}\end{aligned}$$The angles in a triangle sum to 180°.

$\angle CAB=\angle ACB$, so their opposite sides are equal: $BC=AB$. Therefore $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles.

content.prompt: Show that triangle $PQR$ is isosceles, using full reasoning.

answer.short: $\angle QPR=\angle QRP=70^{\circ}$, so $QR=QP$ and $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.
answer.worked:
Angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$:
$$\begin{align*}
\angle QRP &= 180^{\circ}-110^{\circ}\\
\angle QRP &= 70^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
By the exterior angle theorem,
$$\begin{align*}
\angle QPR &= 110^{\circ}-40^{\circ}\\
\angle QPR &= 70^{\circ}.
\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle QPR=\angle QRP$. Sides opposite equal angles are equal, so $QR=QP$ and $\triangle PQR$ is isosceles.

classification.difficultyReason: Straight line, angle sum and equal angles imply an isosceles triangle. A short chain with a written conclusion.

content.prompt: Determine the value of $a$ in this diagram. Explain your reasoning.

answer.worked:
Opposite sides are parallel, so $AD\parallel BC$. Alternate angles on these parallel sides give the angle between the diagonal and the left side as $40^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ADB&=40^\circ&&\text{(alternate angles, }AD\parallel BC\text{)}\\\angle ABD+110^\circ+40^\circ&=180^\circ&&\text{(angle sum of a triangle)}\\\angle ABD&=30^\circ\\a&=30^\circ&&\text{(alternate angles, }AB\parallel DC\text{)}\end{align*}$$

The co-interior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$, so $AB$ is parallel to $DC$ by the converse of the co-interior angle property.

content.prompt: The diagonals of rhombus $ABCD$ meet at $E$.

answer.worked: The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles, so $\angle AEB=90^\circ$.

The diagonals bisect each other.
$$\begin{align*}AE&=30\div2=15\text{ cm}\\BE&=16\div2=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

$\triangle AEB$ is right-angled at $E$ and $AB$ is its hypotenuse. By Pythagoras’ theorem,
$$\begin{align*}AB^2&=15^2+8^2\\AB^2&=225+64\\AB^2&=289\\AB&=17\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$

answer.short: a) $90^\circ$; b) $AE=15\text{ cm}$, $BE=8\text{ cm}$; c) $17\text{ cm}$

content.prompt: Determine the size of the unknown angle in each quadrilateral.

answer.worked:
The $230^\circ$ reflex angle is an interior angle. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+230&=360\\a+310&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

The $130^\circ$ angle is outside the quadrilateral, so the interior angle at that vertex is $360-130=230^\circ$. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+230&=360\\a+310&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.

The $(2a+30)^\circ$ angle is outside the quadrilateral, so the interior angle at that vertex is $360-(2a+30)=330-2a$. The interior angles of a quadrilateral sum to $360^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}a+45+35+(330-2a)&=360\\410-a&=360\\a&=50\end{align*}$$
Therefore, $a=50^\circ$.
